newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends volatile session mainly firmer.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends volatile session mainly firmer.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mainly firmer in rollercoaster dealings on Thursday, but a round of speculative profit taking knocked prices from fresh life-of-contract highs set earlier in the day, traders said.
"Today the market was moved around by speculators," one trader said. "There is a lot of volatility and it is a very difficult market right now."
Most-active May coffee rose 0.10 cent per lb on the day, to end at 166.40 cents, after peaking at a new contract high of 173.00 cents. The session low was 162.00 cents.
Spot March coffee ended up 3.15 cents, to 178.45 cents, but well off its new contract high of 183.50 cents. The back months finished 4.25 higher to 2.75 lower.
Prices headed higher at the outset, defying pre-opening expectations, boosted by trade and speculative buying amid persistent nearby supply concerns, dealers said.
With the spot March contract entering first notice day Thursday, traders said the fact that no delivery notices were issued today compounded supply woes.

March open interest remained high at 5,587 lots as of Wednesday, while stocks of coffee certified by the exchange for delivery stood at 20,795 60-kg bags, the equivalent of about 80 lots. An additional 6,250 bags were pending grading, the CSCE reported after the close.
"Where is the coffee that is going to be delivered?" said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "There is not any out there."
The nearby March/May spread, a barometer of near-term availability, ballooned to 12.05 cent, up from 9.00 cents at the close Wednesday.
Although the spread held firm, the market failed to hang on to gains. Prices fell quickly from new highs after speculators, led by commission houses, moved to take profits.
"It bounced back and forth like the stock market does," said Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka. "I would be somewhat weary, but the underlying fundamentals have not changed and those are bullish."
"Stocks of arabica coffees remain tight and do not show much sign that they will increase significantly," he added.

Technically, one trader said the May contract's close below 168.00 cents was disappointing. May near-term chart support was seen at 160.00 cents, followed by 155.00 cents. On the upside, the contract high of 173.00 cents was pegged as resistance.
Volume on Thursday reached an estimated 18,220 lots, off from Wednesday's official tally of 22,700 lots.
